statement: A bus has 26 passengers. At the first stop, 9 get off and 5 get on. At the second stop, 7 get off and 12 get on. How many passengers are on the bus now?

choices.misconception: I worked out the first stop correctly but forgot about the second stop.
I mixed up the two kinds: I added the people who got off and took away the people who got on.
I mixed up getting on and off at the first stop, but did the second stop correctly.
I added every number in the problem, as if everyone who got off also stayed on.

hints: People getting off make the number smaller.
Go one stop at a time: take away the people who get off, then add the people who get on.
After the first stop there are $26 - 9 + 5 = 22$ passengers.

solutions.reliable: First stop: $26 - 9 + 5 = 22$. Second stop: $22 - 7 + 12 = 27$. The transferable idea: follow the story in order, one change at a time.
solutions.elegant: Altogether $9 + 7 = 16$ got off and $5 + 12 = 17$ got on, so the bus gained 1 passenger: $26 + 1 = 27$.

whyOnTest: A multi-step story where each step changes the total, testing careful tracking of increases and decreases.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
